final.narration: Flow rate equals water velocity times cross-sectional area (Q = V × A); a rating curve assumes this holds at every stage. Since the 2024-10-28 visit, measurements at the French Broad River near Newport, USGS 03455000, sit 46 % below the rating, so published flows run that much too high. For a given flow rate, the river stands 0.71 ft higher than the curve predicts; at a stage of 2.70 ft it carries about 1,350 cfs (42 %) less than the curve's 3,210 cfs. The hydrographer noted "Fill control changed" on 2024-10-28. In the note's terms, gravel built up on the control (the riffle just downstream that sets the water level), so water backs up at the gauge: deeper, more area, much lower velocity. After the change, at that stage, area rose 25 % and velocity fell 58 %, so the flow rate there fell about 48 %, which agrees with the 42 % drop in measured flow rate. Hurricane Helene (2024-09-27) passed between the 2024-08-19 and 2024-10-28 visits; the storm gaugings were rated Poor, the largest 91,700 cfs on 2024-09-28. DriftWatch's agents rank fill / aggradation first (83 %); the Skeptic accepted it. Double-check: Survey the control and apply a negative shift. Rating confidence 30/100 (Stale).
